Infinite scrolling is neither universally good nor bad; its effectiveness depends on context and trade-offs. Benefits include increased user engagement and lower interaction cost for continuous content and mobile use [d1][d3][d4]. However, it can exclude users with disabilities, frustrate users by removing pagination, and induce overuse or anxiety [d2][d5][d6][d8][d9]. The technique works well for discovery interfaces and social feeds but fails for tasks requiring precise navigation or accessibility [d1][d4][d7]. Whether it is “good” hinges on aligning the design with user needs, content characteristics, and ethical considerations.
